title: A fin de cuentas: la conclusión general tras considerar todo

sections.content: A fin de cuentas (in the end, when all is said and done) draws a general conclusion after weighing everything already discussed -- a natural closing move for balanced, synthesis-style writing. It can open or interrupt a sentence, usually set off by commas. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Los presidentes gobiernan, a fin de cuentas, como si el voto popular les otorgara un mandato prácticamente ilimitado.
items.english: Presidents govern, when all is said and done, as if the popular vote granted them a virtually unlimited mandate.

items.spanish: A fin de cuentas, muchas de estas democracias lograron consolidar elecciones periódicas y relativamente limpias.
items.english: In the end, many of these democracies managed to establish periodic, relatively clean elections.

items.spanish: A fin de cuentas, estas democracias imperfectas sentaron las bases de la política latinoamericana posterior.
items.english: In the end, these imperfect democracies laid the groundwork for Latin America's later politics.

items.spanish: El debate fue intenso, pero, a fin de cuentas, ambas partes reconocieron la necesidad de llegar a un acuerdo.
items.english: The debate was intense, but, in the end, both sides recognized the need to reach an agreement.

sections.content: A fin de cuentas works well to wrap up a paragraph that has already presented both strengths and weaknesses -- it signals here's the bottom line after everything just said, similar to en definitiva but with a slightly more conversational, summing-up feel.
